Surrey Heath's population increased by around 4,300 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 90,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Surrey Heath increased by 5.0%, from just over 86,100 in 2011 to around 90,500 in 2021.

The population here increased by a smaller percentage than the overall population of the South East (7.5%), and by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Surrey Heath was home to around 6.8 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 6.5 in 2011. This area was close to the median population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was lower in Surrey Heath than across the South East

An older Surrey Heath

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Surrey Heath increased by two years, from 41 to 43 years of age.

This area had a higher average (median) age than the South East as a whole in 2021 (41 years) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by just over 2,500 (an increase of 15.3%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by around 1,900 (9.4% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.9 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Surrey Heath stood out from other areas for housing

The percentage of households in the social rented sector increased in Surrey Heath, but fell across England.

In Surrey Heath, the percentage of households in the social rented sector rose from 9.2% in 2011 to 9.6% in 2021, while across England it fell from 17.7% to 17.1%. During the same period, the regional percentage fell from 13.7% to 13.6%.

Private renting in Surrey Heath increased from 12.1% to 15.4%, while the rate of home ownership decreased from 76.8% to 74.0%.

The rate of social renting in Surrey Heath increased by 0.4 percentage points

Fewer couples with dependent children

Surrey Heath saw the South East's joint third-largest percentage-point fall (alongside Gosport) in the proportion of households including a couple with dependent children (from 25.4% in 2011 to 23.4% in 2021).

Across the region, only Isle of Wight (from 16.2% to 13.5%) and Rushmoor (from 24.5% to 22.0%) saw a greater decrease in the percentage of households including a couple with dependent children.

Despite the decrease, Surrey Heath was in the highest 10% of English local authority areas for the share of households including a couple with dependent children in 2021.

The percentage of households including a couple with dependent children in Surrey Heath decreased by 2.0 percentage points

Unpaid care in Surrey Heath

In 2021, 4.3% of Surrey Heath residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.1% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, 1.3% of residents (aged five years and over) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.0% in 2011. The proportion of Surrey Heath residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care increased from 1.7% to 1.9%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Surrey Heath (2.8 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South East (2.8 percentage points, from 7.3% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Surrey Heath decreased by 2.8 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Surrey Heath

In 2021, 8.9% of Surrey Heath residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 6.3% in 2011. The 2.7 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the South East, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 5.2% to 7.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 85.0% of people in Surrey Heath identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 90.2% in 2011), while 2.7% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 1.9% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 0.7% in 2011 to 1.8% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 8.9% of usual residents in Surrey Heath identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category

Religion in Surrey Heath

In 2021, 36.0% of Surrey Heath residents reported having "No religion", up from 23.9% in 2011. The rise of 12.1 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Surrey Heath. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the South East, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.7% to 40.2%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 50.0% of people in Surrey Heath described themselves as Christian (down from 63.4%), while 5.7% did not state their religion (down from 7.2% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 36.0% of usual residents in Surrey Heath reported having "No religion"

Change in employment

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed was greater in Surrey Heath (3.1 percentage points) than in nearby Woking (0.9 percentage points).

In Surrey Heath, the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) decreased from 63.3% in 2011 to 60.2% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage in nearby Woking decreased from 63.0% to 62.1%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were unemployed (excluding full-time students) in Surrey Heath fell from 2.5% to 2.4%, while the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were retired (economically inactive) increased from 21.1% to 23.0%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Surrey Heath decreased by 3.1 percentage points

Surrey Heath residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 72,100 Surrey Heath residents said they were born in England. This represented 79.7% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 71,300 in 2011, which at the time represented 82.7% of Surrey Heath's population.

Scotland was the next most represented, with around 1,600 Surrey Heath residents reporting this country of birth (1.7%). This figure was down from around 1,900 in 2011, which at the time represented 2.2% of the population of Surrey Heath.

The number of Surrey Heath residents born in South Africa rose from around 800 in 2011 (1.0% of the local population) to just over 1,300 in 2021 (1.4%).

In 2021, 79.7% of Surrey Heath residents reported their country of birth as England

Fewer adults working long hours

Surrey Heath saw the South East's second-largest percentage-point fall in the proportion of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked over 49 hours per week (from 16.9% in 2011 to 12.9% in 2021).

Across the region, only Bracknell Forest saw a greater fall in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked over 49 hours per week (from 15.8% to 11.7%).

Every local authority area across the South East saw a fall in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked over 49 hours per week, as the regional percentage fell from 14.6% to 11.9%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults in employment who worked 49 hours or more in Surrey Heath decreased by 4.0 percentage points

National identity in Surrey Heath

In 2021, 7.5% of Surrey Heath residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 6.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 50 people (2.2%) identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 1.2% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Surrey Heath that identified as "British only" increased from 19.2% to 58.0%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater across the South East (1.6 percentage points, from 7.1% to 8.7%) than in Surrey Heath (0.9 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Surrey Heath increased by 0.9 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Surrey Heath residents aged 16 years and over, 30.1% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 27.1% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in two people (53.1%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 56.4% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Surrey Heath that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 8.0% to 8.6%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership in Surrey Heath (3.0 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the South East (2.9 percentage points, from 31.9% to 34.8%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Surrey Heath increased by 3.0 percentage points

Disability in Surrey Heath

In 2021, 4.8% of Surrey Heath residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 5.7% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just over 1 in 12 people (8.5%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 8.0% in 2011. The proportion of Surrey Heath residents who were not disabled increased from 86.4% to 86.7%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Surrey Heath (0.9 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South East (1.0 percentage points, from 7.2% to 6.2%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Surrey Heath decreased by 0.9 percentage points

Health in Surrey Heath

In 2021, 54.1% of Surrey Heath residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 51.9% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 33.9% to 32.9%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Surrey Heath residents describing their health as "very bad" was 0.7% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 2.7% to 2.4%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Surrey Heath increased by 2.2 percentage points
